hints.content:
A reflection moves a point perpendicularly across a line, so that the [[☃ definition 3]] is the same distance from the line as the [[☃ definition 4]], but on the other side.



[[☃ image 1]]

In other words, the line of reflection is the perpendicular bisector between any pair of corresponding points in the image and the pre-image.

options.definition: The figure *after* one or more transformations

options.alt: Point R is reflected across a line to form point R prime. Segment R R prime is perpendicular to the line.

hints.content:
Since the $y$-axis is *vertical*, the reflection will move each point of quadrilateral $ABCD$ *horizontally* across the axis.

For example, point $B$ is $3$ units to the right of the $y$-axis, so $B'$ will be $3$ units to the left of the axis.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Quadrilateral A B C D with point A at two, negative three, point B at three, negative six, point C at five, negative four, and point D at four, negative two. A dashed arrow points at both point B prime at negative three, negative six and point B.
